title: Establish SLOs and rollout gates for fast-fail protection and degraded-routing behavior
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: We need a clear, actionable set of SLOs and rollout gates that enable fast-fail protection and deterministic degraded-routing behavior for latency-sensitive interactive workloads. Motivation: during spikes and partial infra degradation (cold KV cache, high kernel queueing, regional capacity loss) we want predictable behavior: quick failover to a degraded route or cheaper model variant, controlled throttling, and automated rollback of releases that increase user-visible latency or error rates. Scope: define numerical SLOs (latency percentiles and availability) for two workload classes (interactive streaming first-byte and completion tail), error budget policies, and rollout gate checks that include cache warmness, cache-hit-rate, GPU utilization, and burn-rate based guards. Deliverables: PRD with numeric SLOs and rationale, rollout gate matrix, dashboard panels for per-route SLOs, CI/CD gating definitions (canary thresholds and automated rollback triggers), updated runbook and stakeholder sign-offs. Out of scope: deep runtime implementation details (those will be handled by ENG tickets), billing changes, and enterprise SLA contract language.
acceptance_criteria: PRD published in Confluence that lists numeric SLOs for both workload classes and explains the rationale (p50/p95/p99 and first-byte targets)
Define availability SLO and monthly error budget (e.g., 99.95% availability with a monthly error budget of 22 minutes) and unit-test style examples of budget burn scenarios
Rollout gate matrix documented that specifies canary thresholds, burn-rate triggers, and cache-warmth gates (minimum KV cache hit-rate thresholds per route)
Console dashboards updated: per-route SLO panels (p50/p95/p99, availability, error budget consumption) and a rollouts overview panel showing gate pass/fail history
CI/CD pipeline includes automated gating: canary must pass all gates for 4 continuous hours with <20% of allowed burn rate and max p99 < defined threshold before wider rollout
Automated rollback policy implemented in ops runbook: rollback when p99 exceeds threshold for 15 minutes AND error budget depletion exceeds 50% within 1 hour
Runbook and escalation matrix updated and reviewed by SRE, runtime, and customer success teams
Stakeholder sign-off captured from Runtime, SRE, Product, and Solutions Engineering on the PRD and rollout gates

notes: Decision point: whether degraded route returns a cheaper model variant (quantized) or an explicit user-facing degraded message. Engineering prefers automated fallback to quantized variant for continuity; CS prefers explicit messaging for enterprise SLAs.
Trade-off: aggressive fast-fail reduces user-visible errors but can raise cost by routing to fallback variants. Need to quantify unit cost impact as follow-up engagement with Finance/Cost Ops.

Instrumentation required: per-request cache_warmness flag, model_variant label, route_tag, and precise token-level latency traces to accurately evaluate p99. ENG tickets will include schema changes for events.
Follow-ups: create ENG tickets for (1) rollout gating automation, (2) dashboard panels, (3) SLO alerting rules, (4) automated rollback hook tied to deployment pipeline.
